title: CheatAgent: Attacking LLM-Empowered Recommender Systems via LLM Agent

problem.claim: The safety vulnerability of LLM-empowered recommender systems remains under-investigated.

gap.claim: Traditional reinforcement-learning attack agents are ineffective against LLM-empowered recommender systems because they have limited capabilities for processing complex textual inputs, planning, and reasoning.

contributions.claim: CheatAgent is an LLM-based attack framework for attacking LLM-empowered recommender systems.
The method identifies an insertion position for maximum impact with minimal input modification and generates adversarial perturbations for that position.
Prompt tuning uses iterative feedback from the victim recommender system to improve attacking strategies and perturbation quality.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe CheatAgent as a novel attack framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments across three real-world datasets demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed attacking method.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM-empowered recommender systems have advanced personalized user experience and attracted attention.
Their safety vulnerability is under-investigated, motivating attacks on black-box systems under security and privacy constraints.
CheatAgent uses an LLM-based agent to locate impactful insertion positions, generate adversarial perturbations, and iteratively improve attack strategies through prompt tuning and victim feedback.
The authors report effectiveness in experiments on three real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: An attack agent can combine position selection, adversarial perturbation generation, and iterative feedback from the victim system.

interpretation.claim: Attack effectiveness may depend on coordinating where to modify inputs, what perturbations to generate, and how to adapt from system feedback.

application.claim: This pattern could inform evaluation workflows for black-box recommender-system robustness.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify which attack settings, datasets, baselines, or failure cases support transfer to other systems.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the three datasets.
The abstract does not report quantitative results or comparison baselines.
The abstract does not specify the attack target, perturbation constraints, or victim recommender-system implementations.
